text:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT detected: streaming tail-latency spike on /v1/stream/gen in eu-west (p95 and p99 SLO breaches). Start time 2026-03-15T14:06:00Z. Paging oncall.
Anna (oncall): I'm oncall, picking this up. Any immediate customer alerts?
Ryan (sre): Seeing proxy 502/504s and long write latencies. p95 ~ 1.8s -> 4.5s, p99 ~ 12s for streaming responses. Error rate spike started ~14:05 UTC.
Maya (eng-runtime): Looking at runtime traces — backend inference nodes showing long stalls on kv-cache flush; many requests accumulate in output queue. Suspect client-side backpressure causing sockets to stall, GC-ish stalls on some inferencers.
Luis (platform): Noticed a sudden increase in long-lived WS connections from tenant boxcorp: ~20k concurrent connections holding open for extended periods. Proxy connection pool saturation + keepalive accumulation.
Customer Success: CS reported elevated error rates for workflows using streaming attachments; two paying customers impacted (BoxCorp, FinFlow). CS opened tickets and informed customers.
Anna (oncall): Confirmed customer impact: intermittent chunking delays and incomplete streams reported. Severity: high for affected tenants.
Ryan (sre): Quick triage options: 1) tighten proxy keepalive/idle timeout to drop slow consumers; 2) apply client-level throttle for connections over threshold; 3) route heavy tenants to degraded non-streaming fallback. Recommend 1 + 3 as fastest.
Maya (eng-runtime): I can roll a fallback that forces chunked buffering -> single response for heavy tenants (less efficient but avoids tail stalls). Prep in canary.
Anna (oncall): Proceed with timed mitigations. I'll coordinate deploys and CS comms.
Anna (oncall): Running command to update proxy keepalive (applying to eu-west pool):
```
kubectl -n platform patch configmap proxy-settings --patch '{"data":{"keepalive_timeout":"20s"}}'
# then rollout restart deploy/proxy-eu-west
```
Anna (oncall): Applying now.
IncidentBot: Deploy bot: proxy-settings patch submitted by Anna. Rolling update started: proxies 0/6 -> 3/6 updated.
Ryan (sre): Patching proxy gives immediate drop in long-lived sockets. Observed EPIPE/WARNs as old conns torn down, throughput recovers for many clients. p95 down to ~300ms after partial rollout. p99 improved but still ~4s.
Maya (eng-runtime): Canary for fallback routing deployed to 10% of boxcorp traffic: route-> non-streaming chunk-mode. Initial telemetry shows reduced backpressure on inferencers and fewer long tail stalls.
Luis (platform): Also enabled connection cap per IP for that tenant and queue-length limit in proxy for streaming endpoints.
Customer Success: BoxCorp engineering acknowledged issue and will update their client to flush more frequently and drop idle listeners. They requested continued throttling while they fix.
Ryan (sre): Collecting traces for postmortem: sample trace IDs: trace-34a7, trace-34a8, trace-35b0 — see dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/traces?ids=34a7,34a8,35b0
Maya (eng-runtime): Added a short-term KV cache warmup to reduce backend calls during bursts. Deployed to inferencer group b.
Anna (oncall): Monitoring for 20 minutes. If stable, mark mitigated -> monitoring. Creating follow-up ticket to remove tenant-specific throttles and implement long-term fixes: better streaming backpressure controls, smarter proxy backoff, tenant throttling policies, and docs for customer client behaviour.
Ryan (sre): Notes for postmortem: investigate why socket teardown wasn't shedding load fast enough (connection refs held in proxy write loop), review proxy write buffer sizing, and add alerts for sustained long-lived connections per tenant.
IncidentBot: STATUS UPDATE: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident lead: Anna (oncall). Escalation complete.
Anna (oncall): Thanks all. I'll hand over to Maya & Ryan for postmortem and remediation plan. :thumbsup:
